subject: biology

hotspots.label: Nuclear envelope
hotspots.description: A double membrane that wraps the nucleus and separates its contents from the cytoplasm. It is studded with pores.
hotspots.positionHint: The rounded outer rim of the nucleus, at the upper right edge.
hotspots.function: Separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm while controlling what passes through its pores.

hotspots.label: Nuclear pore
hotspots.description: An opening in the nuclear envelope that acts like a controlled door, letting messages and materials through.
hotspots.positionHint: On the front face of the envelope, below the nucleolus toward the viewer.
hotspots.function: Controls the movement of RNA copies and building materials between nucleus and cytoplasm.

hotspots.label: Nucleolus
hotspots.description: A dense, darker sphere inside the nucleus that assembles the parts used to build ribosomes.
hotspots.positionHint: Interior center, slightly low, shown via a clipped half of the nucleus.
hotspots.function: Assembles the RNA components that become part of ribosomes.

hotspots.label: Nucleoplasm
hotspots.description: The fluid filling the nucleus, along with the scattered chromatin (DNA + proteins).
hotspots.positionHint: Spread across the interior volume of the nucleus.
hotspots.function: Provides the medium in which the DNA (chromatin) sits and the nucleolus floats.

visualStyleNotes: Anatomy Atelier bar throughout: warm off-white/paper background (#F7F3EC) with a soft radial vignette, no floor grid, no scene props. The nucleus floats large and centered, lit with soft neutral studio light, no bloom or emissive anywhere. Restrained color: the nucleus is a calm warm-paper sphere, the envelope slightly deeper warm-taupe than the nucleoplasm, the nucleolus faint amber, the DNA/chromatin threads a softened muted rust. Strong saturated color reserved only for the small flat hotspot dots.
materialNotes: Metallic-roughness PBR, metallic=0, roughness ~0.5-0.65 matte. The envelope may have a subtle translucent fresnel (alpha ~0.85) so interior structures read, but keep it soft and semi-opaque - not glassy. No emissive anywhere.
assetBrief: SUBJECT: The nucleus of a eukaryotic cell as a self-contained study model (the cytoplasm is a faint transparent hint only, not the focus). Build a rounded nucleus {~1.6 units across) shown one half removed (clean flat cross-section cap, museum-model style, no gore) to reveal the interior. Inside: an outer double nuclear envelope (two nested shells, the inner shell slightly inset), wave-like strands of chromatin (DNA) curving through the interior, and one dense nucleolus sphere off-center. Scatter a few visible pore rings across the envelope surface. Materials follow the parallel background/paper and muted warm-tau palette; the chromatin is a pale desaturated grey, the nucleolus soft amber, all near-neutral. Do not use saturated 'legend' colors on the mesh; keep them for hotspot dots only. No glow, no emissive, no floor. Named nodes: OuterEnvelope, InnerEnvelope, ChromatinThreads, NucleolusMesh, Pore_Ring01 etc., CytoplasmContext (optional transparent shell). Budget 8-15k triangles. camera framing leaves generous negative space; auto-rotate slow and on by default.
referenceMatch: Match the render, lighting and composition of assets/reference/anatomy-atelier/desktop-overview.png - object floats alone on a warm off-white radial-vignette ground, no props, generous negative space for the hotspot-card UI.
